Alicia: heads-up: noticed a parity issue between the TS SDK and REST embeddings batch endpoint. When sending duplicate inputs, the SDK returns embeddings in the order the server processed them, but the REST response includes an explicit input_index mapping. sample-service relies on stable ordering and now mismatches duplicates.

Priya: can you paste a tiny repro? which sdk version?

Alicia: repro (ts, sdk@3.1.0):
```ts
const inputs = ["foo","bar","foo"]
const res = await client.embeddings.batch({ model: 'embed-small', inputs })
// SDK res.embeddings -> [emb_foo_1, emb_bar, emb_foo_2]
// but sample-service maps by position and expects the middle to be for "bar" which is fine, but duplicates lose traceability when downstream dedup/attribution runs
```

Alicia: curl to REST shows explicit mapping: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings/batch -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"inputs":["foo","bar","foo"]}'
# -> {"data":[{"input_index":0,"embedding":[...]},{"input_index":2,"embedding":[...]},{"input_index":1,"embedding":[...]}]
# server indicates processing order but includes input_index for correct alignment
```

Theo: oh interesting. so SDK flattens/normalizes to an array in processing order but drops input_index. that breaks idempotent downstream pipelines that dedupe by content but then need to map back to original positions.

Jamie: is the SDK intentionally dropping input_index? it might have been trying to present a simpler array for common cases. but parity should preserve all server metadata.

Priya: workaround: sample-service will call REST directly and use input_index to rebuild order. but this defeats the point of using SDK. we should fix the SDK.

Alicia: logs: "200 POST /v1/embeddings/batch -> normalized to embeddings[] (dropped data[].input_index)"

Jamie: opened RED-5189. Proposed SDK change: 1) expose full server "data" array as returned (including input_index) under response.raw or response.items, 2) keep convenience .embeddings array but populate it using input_index to preserve original ordering, 3) document behavior for duplicate inputs. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-sdk/pull/1210 (WIP).

Theo: also add an integration test with duplicates and assert that mapping by input_index recovers original positions. and add a small migration note: consumers relying on processing-order-only semantics might observe reorder.

Priya: agree. FYI some teams relied on SDK returning processing-order for latency reasons. adding an opt-in flag `preserveServerOrder=true|false` seems reasonable but default should be safe: preserve original input order and expose server processing order separately.

Jamie: plan: change default in next patch 3.1.1, include raw.items & preserve ordering. sample-service will switch back to SDK once released. ETA: tomorrow AM for canary.

ops-bot: Created issue RED-5189 and assigned to @Jamie. Priority: P2.

Alicia: thanks — patch will make debugging a lot easier. :thumbsup:
